messages.author: 9c5e1e585b3eafe0
messages.subject: Multiple Bar Plot
parts:
Dear all,

First of all, ggplot2 is amazing!

However, I am a newbie, and as every newbie I have a problem
I want to plot more than 2 bars of different variables but with same
characteristics (there will be one legend) in the same plot

What I mean:
I want these two bars in the same plot

qplot("Food", data = simple, geom="bar", position="fill",
fill = ModeFor.FoodShop.) + coord_flip() +
scale_fill_discrete('Mode') + scale_x_discrete("Food Shopping") +
scale_y_continuous("")

qplot("Work", data = simple, geom="bar", position="fill",
fill = ModeFor.Work.) + coord_flip() +
scale_fill_discrete('Mode') + scale_x_discrete("Work") +
scale_y_continuous("")

I've also tried this:

qplot(c("Work", "FoodShopping"), data = simple, geom="bar",
position="fill",
fill =XXXXX ) + coord_flip() +
scale_fill_discrete('Mode') + scale_x_discrete("Work/School") +
scale_y_continuous("")

Where XXXXX must be respectively 'k1' for the 'Work' variable and
'k2' for the 'FoodShopping'

However, ggplot2 does now allow me to choose more than one 'fill'

Any suggestions?

Thanks a lot!

messages.author: 9ff02ee016b8a9e0
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Bar Plot
parts:
You did not provide reproducible data...however,...



is this example what you want?
qplot(factor(cyl), data=mtcars, geom="bar", fill=factor(cyl))
or if those variables you want in the same graph with different fills, you could melt the data frame so that the two variables become one with an id variable that could be used as fill=id
